raw_text:
This node is a REGRESSION PIN, and it says so: the behaviour the goal names was already present at base 5a3372c2, reckon/ is byte-identical between base and head, and the deliverable is the case that would now fail if the behaviour regressed. It is judged as a pin, not marked down for an implementation that was correctly not written.

MEASURE m1 (the fetch age is a field a caller reads, not only the detail string): ASSERTED, and shown to fire. tests/test_cached_account_age.py:114-118 asserts fetch_age_seconds on the returned block, its arithmetic agreement with the block's own ISO stamp, and that the detail string is not the only carrier.
MEASURE m2 (a cached reading whose fetch stamp cannot be resolved is unknown and never shows a bare figure): ASSERTED. tests/test_cached_account_age.py:154-182 parametrises five stamps across four shapes (absent, unparseable, wrongly typed twice, unzoned) and requires no structure holding a figure and no prose percentage anywhere in the block.
MEASURE m3 (a live reading is unaffected, so the change is not a blanket suppression): ASSERTED at tests/test_cached_account_age.py:185-219, which supplies both a live answer and a cache and requires the live figure with no cache markers on the block.
MEASURE m4 (the fixture is written under a temp path via the environment and the real cache path is asserted untouched): PARTLY ASSERTED. The environment half fires (tests/test_cached_account_age.py:88 asserts the fixture path is under tmp_path). The real-path half at tests/test_cached_account_age.py:259 cannot fail from the path under test, because cached_account_budget takes its path as a parameter, so the byte-comparison guards a file this code never opens. Named as a FINDING.
MEASURE m5 (the declared mutation is applied to a scratch copy, the named test is observed to FAIL, and the log is written to the negative-control path): ASSERTED, and independently reproduced by me. Removing block["fetch_age_seconds"] = round(age, 1) from reckon/_backends.py:677 in a scratch copy of the fixed tree reddened exactly 3 of the 9 cases and left 6 green; my module resolution check printed reckon._backends resolving to the scratch root.
MEASURE-BASE-FACT: every clause of this done_when was already satisfied at base 5a3372c2. Measured, not read: the new file passes 9 of 9 against the base source in a scratch tree, and a recursive byte-comparison of the base and head reckon/ trees reports them identical. The node's own manifest states this plainly rather than claiming an implementation.
